source_read: The same PDFs as the blind round: Clements et al. (1982) printed pp. 539-542; Yanagihara et al. (2003) printed pp. 37-43; Peltoniemi et al. (2016), 19 pages of the online-first PDF. Tables and figures checked on pages rendered at 130 to 300 dpi, the text layer of the 1982 scan being unreliable.

results.corrected_extracted: Because the norketamine areas after the oral and intravenous conditions were similar once corrected for dose, the authors attribute the low oral ketamine concentrations to first-pass metabolism rather than to poor absorption (2nd paragraph); they compare their intravenous half-life with the 151 minutes reported after anaesthetic amounts (2.5 mg/kg) in patients, against 186 minutes at the analgesic amounts studied here (1st paragraph); and they report norketamine concentrations up to 390 ng/mL in some people after the oral solution (4th paragraph, the Results giving the oral range as 80 to 390 ng/mL on the same page).
results.note: Every number holds: 390 ng/mL and 151 against 186 minutes. Only the locator needs widening, since the 390 ng/mL figure is four paragraphs into the Discussion. My blind reading found the same first-pass reading.

results.corrected_locator: Section 6 Pharmacodynamics and Clinical Use of Ketamine, 1st and 2nd paragraphs
results.corrected_extracted: In its 2nd paragraph the review states that the two forms have similar pharmacokinetic profiles but different effects: some studies indicate the S-form may be about four times more potent than the R-form as an analgesic in humans while producing more auditory and visual disturbances, R-ketamine produces more agitation in surgical patients, emergence is faster after S-ketamine than after the R-form or the racemate, and the difference in analgesic efficiency is explained by S-ketamine's four times higher affinity for the NMDA receptor. The 1st paragraph gives effective concentrations for loss of consciousness of 241 ng/mL (SD 90) for the racemate and 111 (SD 30) for S-ketamine, taken from a textbook chapter.
results.note: All four statements and both concentrations verified. The concentrations sit in the section's 1st paragraph, not the 2nd, so the locator needs both. Everything here is the review's report of other studies, and the anchor says so.

Both statements sit in Section 7.2's 1st paragraph on p. 12 as given: the 16.5-fold S-norketamine area, which the review attributes to one study, and metabolites measurable 10 to 30 minutes after ingestion. Role fits.

results.corrected_locator: Table 2, column AUC(0→8h); the interpretation in the Discussion paragraph beginning on p. 42
results.corrected_extracted: Norketamine exposure in three healthy men, (R)- then (S)-enantiomer: 533.8 and 494.9 ng·h/mL after the swallowed tablet, 462.9 and 408.7 after the sublingual tablet, 322.6 and 282.6 after the suppository, 173.8 and 149.8 after the injection, and 115.9 and 100.7 after the nasal spray. The nasal pair is headed as the area to 8 hours in Table 2 but called the area to 6 hours in the abstract and the Discussion, because norketamine was below the detection limit 8 hours after the spray, so that pair is integrated over a shorter window than the other four. The reading that the nasal route largely escapes first-pass metabolism is the authors', stated in the Discussion on p. 42, not in the table.
results.note: All ten values confirmed on the rendered page. Two fixes: the interpretation comes from the Discussion, not Table 2, and the nasal window differs from the rest, which weakens the comparison the anchor supports.

results.corrected_locator: Results, last (4th) paragraph, which begins on p. 39 and ends at the top of the left column of p. 40
results.corrected_extracted: In three healthy men, no pharmacokinetic parameter of ketamine or norketamine differed significantly between the (R)- and the (S)-enantiomer, or between the five preparations, by analysis of variance (named in the Methods on p. 39 with 0.05 as the minimal level of significance). No test statistic, degrees of freedom or p-value is printed anywhere in the paper, so this null result in three people cannot be read as evidence that the two forms behave alike in the body.
results.note: Wording and substance confirmed, including the absence of any test statistic. Only the page changes: the paragraph begins on p. 39, and METHODS section 6.2 counts a paragraph on the page where it starts. Role fits.

results.corrected_locator: Table 2, column AUC(0→8h) (p. 42); Results, last (4th) paragraph (begins p. 39) and Discussion, 2nd paragraph (begins p. 42)
results.corrected_extracted: Norketamine exposure differs sharply by preparation: area to 8 hours 173.8 and 149.8 ng·h/mL for the (R)- and (S)-enantiomer after the 20 mg injection against 533.8 and 494.9 after the 50 mg swallowed tablet, in the same three men. The authors describe the tablet's norketamine area as approximately eight times the ketamine area to infinity and read it as extensive first-pass metabolism; the printed values give 7.4 and 7.6 (editors' recomputation: 533.8 divided by 72.3 and 494.9 divided by 64.9).
results.note: Numbers confirmed. The eight-times statement is not in the Discussion's 1st paragraph (pp. 40-41, the enantiomers); it is in the Results (p. 39) and the Discussion paragraph beginning on p. 42, and rounds 7.4 and 7.6 up.
